newsitem.title: USA: SEC to help investors choose among mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: SEC to help investors choose among mutual funds.

text.p: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt will propose new rules to make it easier for investors to select from the thousands of available mutual funds, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
The announcement, expected Tuesday, would cap several years of effort by the commission to make disclosure documents such as mutual fund prospectuses more readable.
Levitt has expressed concern thatn investors are not getting adequate disclosure of risks involved in stock and bond investing.
The full commission was expected to vote Thursday to issue the three rule proposals for public comment, the Post said, quoting commission sources.
The proposals include a rewriting of the mutual fund prospectus, with the addition of material about funds' risks, it said, quoting commission documents.
To encourage investors to read prospectuses, Levitt will propose relegating less relevant information to a separate document, and to ensure they are written in "plain English."

Levitt was also expected to propose a rule that would allow management companies to sell a fund based on a four-page profile which would summarize the key points on the prospectus, as well as one that bans misleading fund names.
Stock funds will also be required, under the new rules, to have at least 80 percent of their clients' money in equities, up from the 65 percent required currently, the Post said.
